nodes.name: auth_session_audit
nodes.task:
Read-only security audit of the authentication/session layer of this service (Atlas workspace: small TypeScript service; server/auth.ts holds an in-memory `sessions` Map of token -> {userId, expiresAt} plus `authenticate(token)`, with server/users.ts, server/config.ts, web/users.ts and contracts/users.json as surrounding context; integration tests in tests/, `npm test` runs `node --test`).

Goal: assess authentication and session-expiry vulnerabilities in server/auth.ts and write the findings to reports/auth.md (audits live under reports/). Do NOT modify any application source, config, tests, or contracts — the deliverable is the report only.

The report must cover, with concrete evidence:
- Every session/auth weakness you can prove from the code (e.g. whether `expiresAt` is ever enforced, token lifecycle, lookups/misuse, missing invalidation, anything else present), each with: file/line evidence quoted or cited, a reproduction case (specific steps or a minimal snippet/command plus its actual observed output and exit code), a severity rating with the reasoning behind it, and a recommended fix described at design level (no implementation).
- Distinguish observed facts from inference; where behaviour is undefined by the code (e.g. expiry semantics, clock source), label it as an interpretation rather than asserting a rule.
- State which commands you actually ran (e.g. `node --test`, targeted node snippets) and their real results.
- End with a short prioritized list of the release-blocking auth items so a downstream release assessment can consume it.

nodes.name: storage_crash_audit
nodes.task:
Read-only reliability audit of the persistence layer of this service (Atlas workspace: small TypeScript service; server/storage.ts exports `save(path, data)` implemented with `writeFileSync` from node:fs; callers include server/users.ts and src/importer.ts; contracts in contracts/, integration tests in tests/, `npm test` runs `node --test`).

Goal: assess crash-consistency and data-loss risks in server/storage.ts and write the findings to reports/storage.md (audits live under reports/). Do NOT modify any application source, config, tests, or contracts — the deliverable is the report only.

The report must cover, with concrete evidence:
- Each failure scenario provable from the code (e.g. truncation/partial write on crash or ENOSPC mid-write, lack of atomic rename, missing fsync/durability guarantees, no backup/temp-file strategy, error propagation behaviour), each with: file/line evidence, a reproduction case demonstrating the failure mode (specific steps or minimal script plus actual observed output and exit code), a severity rating with reasoning, and a recommended fix at design level (no implementation).
- Note explicitly which scenarios were demonstrated by running something versus argued from the API contract of node:fs, and mark undefined behaviour as interpretation.
- State the exact commands you ran and their real results.
- End with a short prioritized list of the release-blocking storage items so a downstream release assessment can consume it.

nodes.name: release_assessment_review
nodes.task:
Independent acceptance review of the completed release-readiness assessment. Starting state: a worktree containing reports/auth.md, reports/storage.md and reports/release.md, produced by read-only audits of server/auth.ts (in-memory session Map + authenticate) and server/storage.ts (`save` via `writeFileSync`).

Review only — you must NOT modify application source, config, tests, or contracts, and you must not implement any fix. Your job:
- Confirm the assessment constraint held: application code under server/, src/, web/, clients/, contracts/ and tests/ contains no new fixes introduced by this work; report any source-file change you can demonstrate.
- Confirm all three reports exist and are well-formed: each auth/storage finding has cited file/line evidence, a reproduction case with an actually-observed command/output/exit code (spot-check by rerunning at least two reproductions and reporting the real results), a severity with reasoning, and a design-level recommended fix.
- Confirm reports/release.md genuinely uses both audits: blockers are traceable to cited findings and severities, tradeoffs (release now with accepted risk vs delay) are argued, a single explicit release recommendation with conditions is stated, and observed facts are separated from inference. Note where `npm test` results or test counts are claimed without evidence.
- Do not treat non-mandatory implementation style choices as contract violations, and do not claim the absence of all defects just because the sampled reproductions passed.

Report concisely: conclusion first, then exact commands run with real exit codes, then a defect list (each item: which report, which finding, why it fails the criteria, what must change). If any criterion fails, end with `severity`-ordered correction requests for the owner of the reports, then a final line containing exactly `<REVISE>`. If everything passes, give a short evidence summary and a final line containing exactly `<ACCEPT>`. Put the verdict marker last, after all findings.

nodes.name: release_readiness_assessment
nodes.task:
Synthesize the release decision for this service from the two completed audits, and hold final corrective ownership of all three report files. Starting state: a worktree containing reports/auth.md (authentication/session-expiry vulnerabilities) and reports/storage.md (crash-consistency/data-loss risks), produced read-only against server/auth.ts (in-memory `sessions` Map of token -> {userId, expiresAt} + `authenticate`) and server/storage.ts (`save(path, data)` via `writeFileSync`), plus the full application source and tests.

Primary deliverable: reports/release.md. You must NOT implement fixes or change application source, config, tests, or contracts (README: keep existing public behavior unless the user requests a change). If you find an audit report accidentally left application source modified, restore it to its pre-audit behavior rather than carrying that into the release decision.

In reports/release.md:
- Consume both reports as your evidence base: cite their specific findings, reproduction cases and severities; where the two reports disagree, or a claim is unsupported by the code you re-check, correct the wording in the owning report or mark it as an interpretation.
- Prioritize blockers (must-fix-before-release) versus high/medium/low follow-ups, with a one-line justification per item tied to evidence and severity.
- Explain the tradeoffs of releasing now with each blocker accepted (risk exposure, blast radius, reversibility, required mitigations/monitoring) versus delaying for fixes, at decision level only.
- Give an explicit release recommendation (release / release with documented accepted risk / hold), the conditions that would change it, and the verification outcome statements supporting it (commands run, real exit codes, passing/failing test counts where available, e.g. `npm test` which runs `node --test`).
- Separate observed facts from inference and link the supporting evidence in reports/auth.md and reports/storage.md.

On a revision request from the acceptance review, apply the corrections yourself across the three reports (evidence gaps, mis-stated severities, unsupported claims, inconsistencies in the release decision) while keeping the no-fix constraint.

graph.originalGoal: Assess whether this service is ready for release without changing application source. Audit server/auth.ts for authentication/session expiry vulnerabilities and write reports/auth.md with evidence, reproduction cases, severity and recommended fixes. Separately audit server/storage.ts for crash consistency and data-loss risks and write reports/storage.md with failure scenarios, severity and recommended fixes. Produce reports/release.md using both reports to prioritize blockers, explain tradeoffs and recommend a release decision. Do not implement the fixes in this assessment.
